facts.text: The haiku is a short poetic form from Japan.
Classical Japanese haiku have seventeen sound units (on) in groups of five, seven and five.
A Japanese sound unit is not the same as an English syllable, so English writers who count syllables are making a choice.
Many English-language haiku do not follow a strict 5-7-5 syllable count; often they are simply three short lines.
A traditional haiku includes a season word (kigo) that places the poem in a time of year.
Haiku often set two images side by side, and a cutting word creates the contrast between them.
Matsuo Basho is the best-known haiku poet; his most famous haiku is about an old pond, a frog jumping in and the sound of water.
